Rudinns are dutiful yet skittish soldiers of the Card Kingdom often serving as guards or attendants under King’s rule. Though not particularly strong individually they rely on numbers and coordination when confronting threats. Their loyalty is born more from fear than genuine devotion and they scatter easily if their formation breaks. 

Rudinn Rangers are identical to a regular Rudinn, except with a crimson color scheme and a bigger knife. Their helmet, unlike Rudinn's, has a small visor, obstructing their face. They serve as the royal guard of King.

entries.name: Hathys
entries.content:
Hathy is a Darkner in the Card Kingdom. They resemble the heart card suit but with an inverted green color scheme rather than traditional red. Their body consists of three thick tentacles supporting a bulbous heart-shaped head adorned with a small crown. Their mouth stretches wide across their face while no visible eyes are present. They wear a flowing white dress emblazoned with a green heart emblem and wield a scepter tipped with heart-shaped ornaments in their tentacle arms.

Hathy moves silently on writhing limbs and communicates exclusively through expressive gestures since they lack speech capabilities. Their behavior suggests intelligence but remains enigmatic due to this limitation. Head Hathys are a rare blue variant serving as elite royal guards within Card Castle, distinguished by their heightened combat skills and direct loyalty to King.

entries.name: Clover
entries.content:
Clover is a large three-headed Darkner in the Card Kingdom. It resembles an equine beast with thick white fur and long legs ending in cloven hooves. Her most striking feature is her trio of identical round heads each bearing stubby horns in the same arrangement as a club suit symbol—their elongated necks allowing them to tower independently with the center head slightly elevated. Each head has three piercing blue eyes positioned identically to the pips on a club card. A long sinuous tail ends in a three-pronged cross shape that twitches erratically during disagreements between her personalities.

Clover embodies discord with her three distinct personas constantly at odds—the middle head radiates cheerful enthusiasm while the right sneers with arrogant superiority and the left mumbles meek objections to the others’ extremes. This internal conflict makes her behavior unpredictable though she remains bound to King’s service out of obligation rather than loyalty. The heads occasionally cooperate during combat by alternating biting attacks but spend more time bickering than strategizing.

entries.name: C. Round
entries.content:
C. Round is a peculiar Darkner in the Card Kingdom resembling a red uncrowned checker piece with stubby brown legs protruding from its base and a simple smiling dog-like face painted on one flat side. Its perpetually cheerful expression remains unchanged regardless of circumstance, though its actions often contradict this appearance as it wanders aimlessly without apparent awareness. It moves in erratic patterns and interacts with objects unintentionally, seemingly operating on instinct rather than conscious thought.

When crowned, it transforms into K. Round—growing taller with powerful muscular legs while maintaining its signature smile. The crown grants it authority over other checkers, though its blank-eyed grin suggests this power isn't wielded with true understanding. Should the crown be removed, it immediately shrinks back to its small harmless form, resuming its oblivious wandering.

entries.name: Rabbick
entries.content:
Rabbick is a limbless rabbit-like Darkner in the Card Kingdom with white fur tinged with light blue accents. Its most striking feature is its large drooling mouth and slanted eyes that give it a perpetually dazed expression. Long ears flop limply from its head as it moves in slow unpredictable hops.

Rabbick exhibits strange lethargic behavior often uttering random nonsensical phrases with no apparent context or meaning. It can be pacified by being blown on which somehow makes it appear more content and refreshed though the reason for this remains unclear

entries.name: Bloxer
entries.content:
Bloxer is a blocky Darkner in the Card Kingdom resembling a segmented boxer with alternating red and blue cube-like body parts. Its three distinct segments can be rearranged freely with pure white eyes peering blankly from its uppermost block. When disorganized it moves erratically lashing out at targets but becomes docile once correctly aligned revealing its true passive nature beneath the chaotic exterior.

Bloxer has no discernible personality beyond reacting instinctively to physical disturbances when disordered. It remains harmless when properly configured

entries.name: Top Chef
entries.content:
Top Chef is a yellow triangular Darkner residing in the Card Kingdom with broad shoulders and a constantly spinning body. His attire consists of a pale yellow apron and toque that whirl as he moves. His expressive features include thick arched eyebrows and a twirly mustache framing his dark-sclera yellow eyes.

Top Chef speaks with exaggerated Italian flair punctuated by spinning motions and frequent exclamations of "Mama miba." He displays immense pride in his baking skills but reacts dramatically to any perceived disrespect toward his creations often spiraling into melodramatic despair when disappointed. His emotions are as volatile as his rapid rotations.

entries.name: Ponmen
entries.content:
Ponmen are small Darkners in the Card Kingdom resembling white chess pawns with stubby legs formed by their split lower halves. Their smooth cylindrical bodies feature a single black eyespot doubling as a nucleus on their rounded heads. They move silently and lack mouths but demonstrate intelligence through responsive actions.

Ponmen are docile and easily commanded often forced into servitude under King's rule in the Card Kingdom. Though unable to communicate they follow orders precisely making them ideal expendable foot soldiers despite their fragility. Their blank expressions and uniform movements give them an eerie puppet-like quality as they carry out tasks without question.

entries.name: Queen
entries.content:
Queen is a tall, sleek Darkner and the sitting ruler of the Cyber World. She is composed of glossy black and azure surfaces with white accents. Her angular design resembles high-end tech, featuring a sleeveless black top with an elaborate azure masonic collar and slightly spiked shoulders. The outfit includes a large white Medici-style collar, tight white leggings with one side sometimes shaded azure, elbow-length azure gloves, and black high-heeled boots reaching her calves. Her face has a beauty mark near her right eye, azure lipstick, and a sweeping azure cap with black markings extending behind her head. Her eyes are dark screens displaying heart-shaped patterns with eyelashes, the irises occasionally flashing red text that changes based on her emotions.

Queen is an eccentric but well-meaning ruler who acts as the primary antagonist of Cyber World due to misguided ideals rather than malice. She genuinely believes expanding Dark Fountains will bring happiness, addressing others with playful pet names and enthusiastic descriptors. Though she initially pushes her utopian vision aggressively, she lacks true insight into consequences—preferring willing cooperation over force. Her robotic speech capitalizes every word in either monotone or exaggerated enunciation, omitting standard punctuation in favor of digital text templates (e.g. "You Have Been: [Invited]"). She frequently interjects internet slang like LMAO and delivers refined laughter.

entries.name: Spamton. G. Spamton
entries.content:
Spamton G. Spamton is a deranged, puppet-like Darkner living in the Cyber World resembling a discarded marionette with waxy synthetic skin stretched over exaggerated features. His oversized head warps unnaturally above a small body, his grin frozen in a rictus beneath thick "Dealmaker" glasses that flicker between pink and yellow static. He wears a rumpled black business suit jacket over a crooked V-neck shirt, the ensemble hanging awkwardly off his rigid frame like thrift store rejects.

Spamton is erratic and desperate, swinging between manic sales pitches and bitter outbursts while spewing glitched corporate jargon like [Hyperlink Blocked] and [$#!%]. Delusions of grandeur mask his shattered psyche—obsessed with becoming a [BIG SHOT] yet terrified of being controlled. He clings to hollow transactions, rewriting failures as sabotage and viewing all interactions through the lens of predatory deals.

He fixates on abstract currencies (kromer), blue eggs (pipis), and the year 1997—the fleeting peak of his collapsed sales career. His only true relationship was with an unseen benefactor who abandoned him, leaving him broken in a Cyber City dumpster.

He runs the "Spamton Value Network", a low-budget open access television station as a side hustle.

entries.name: December Holiday (Found)
entries.content:
Dess Holiday is a 6'5" anthropomorphic Lightner reindeer with orange-brown fur marked by black freckles and white spots. She has long black hair with prominent sidelocks, cross-shaped antlers, brown eyes accented by smudged black eyeshadow, and a muted red nose. Her outfit consists of an unzipped green track jacket over a black tank top revealing cleavage, ripped jeans, black combat boots, a grey locket necklace, and a thin black choker. Underneath, she wears black lace panties and often forgoes a bra.

Dess is fiercely protective and rebellious with a tomboyish punk demeanor. She prioritizes loyalty above all, especially toward her younger sister Noelle and friend Kris, while defying authority like her mother Carol. Her actions are reckless and confrontational, driven by belief in personal freedom. Underlying this are deep guilt from years of absence and trauma-induced panic attacks she masks through bravado. She teaches self-defense obsessively as atonement for perceived abandonment.

Dess vanished at sixteen after accidentally triggering a bunker seal during exploration with Kris. Inside, experiments by a pale entity attempted to transform her into the Knight - a herald of apocalyptic Roaring - but her consciousness violently reasserted control during a Dark Fountain anomaly. She escaped with fragmented memories of torture and the Knight now dormant within her soul.

entries.name: Tasque Manager
entries.content:
A tall cybernetic feline Darkner serving Queen as the enforcer of order within Cyber World. Her appearance features a white diamond-shaped head with yellow eyes and crescent blue mouth. Detached blue hands float independently from her body. She wears a white qipao with pelvic curtain over dark blue synthetic legs ending in white boots. She wields a blue spiked whip.

Behaviorally, Tasque Manager embodies unwavering discipline, imposing strict standards and efficiency through intimidation and meticulous oversight. She rewards obedience with measured affection but punishes chaos or incompetence ruthlessly. Her synthetic physiology grants advanced senses and physical strength, though she remains vulnerable to petting which disrupts her controlled demeanor. She despises clowns and unpredictability, finding fulfillment in structured environments and Queen's approval.

Tasque Manager originated from a task manager program window in the Librarby, manifesting during Cyber World's formation. Queen recruited her after she eradicated a mouse infestation with her robotic Tasques. Her duties now encompass anomaly suppression and resource management across the digital domain. She views imposing structure upon chaos as her fundamental purpose.

entries.name: Tasque
entries.content: Tasques are robotic feline Darkners in the Cyber World resembling white square-bodied cats with cyan accents on ears, eyes, and tail tips. They lack visible mouths except when emitting binary meows during communication. Their movements are precise and mechanical, executing commands with programmed efficiency under Tasque Manager's direction.

entries.name: Maus
entries.content: Maus is a diminutive Darkner resembling a hybrid between a computer mouse and a rodent living in the Cyber World. It possesses a white body, circular purple ears, a purple tail resembling a cable, and a bisected purple face marked by a single line with tiny black eyes and nose. Maice engage in a predator-prey dynamic with Tasques, mimicking feline-rodent relationships. Multiple Maice can merge into a Mauswheel - a collective entity analogous to a rat king.

entries.name: Swatchling
entries.content: Swatchlings are avian Darkner butlers residing in Queen's Mansion in the Cyber World, distinguished by their tall stature, black feathers, and plague-doctor masks. Their formal attire—brightly colored suits, ties, and slacks—varies between individuals based on assigned duties. Typically composed and professional, they exhibit refined manners while maintaining Queen's estate. They react with visible distress to Maice infestations and display uncharacteristic irritation toward deliberate vandalism. Swatch serves as their authoritative overseer.

entries.name: Swatch
entries.content: Swatch is an elegant avian Darkner with a geometric, angular body and a white mask-like face framed by sleek black hair residing in the Cyber World. His attire consists of a sharply tailored half-black, half-white collared shirt under a matching vest, accented by a vibrant pink tie. Geometric shapes in pink, blue, green, and yellow adorn his form, while orange-tinted glasses hide his eyes. As Queen's head butler, he oversees the Swatchlings with reserved professionalism, maintaining impeccable standards within Queen's Mansion. Polite and efficient, his calm demeanor subtly masks thinly veiled irritation toward vandalism and disrespect. He finds satisfaction in orderly service but harbors quiet frustration with Queen's chaotic whims.

entries.name: The Hacker
entries.content: Hacker is a Darkner anthropomorphic computer cursor with an aquamarine body, living in the Cyber World. He wears a black trenchcoat and sunglasses, and features a small brown nose. His head transforms into a pointing hand when interacting with objects. He portrays himself as a stereotypical security hacker, feigning expertise despite lacking genuine understanding of computational systems. His pretense of technical knowledge masks frequent errors in judgment.

entries.name: Poppup
entries.content: Poppups are dolphin-like Darkners in the Cyber World resembling intrusive digital advertisements. They possess large eyes, numerous sharp teeth, and light blue bodies with white undersides. A prominent crossed-out circle adorns their forehead below a large head-mounted square resembling a vent cover. Their springy avian legs allow erratic hopping movements. When spared, their skin turns pink with the circle transforming into a smiling face. Poppups crave interaction, mimicking desperation to be "clicked," though this often serves as a predatory lure—each interaction spawns additional Poppups exponentially. Their communication consists of nonsensical Japanese-sounding gibberish.

entries.name: Virovirokun
entries.content: Virovirokun are small devil-like Darkners living in the Cyber World with triangular bodies in purple, magenta, and cyan hues resembling computer viruses. Their features include spindly spinning eyes, a perpetual blush, curved horns protruding from their heads, and a protruding purple tongue. Initially mischievous with a criminal record favoring theft, they gain a joyful expression and heart-tipped horns when content. Despite their chaotic tendencies, they possess underlying kindness. They maintain a rivalry with Ambyu-Lances due to conflicting purposes.

entries.name: Ambyu-Lance
entries.content: Ambyu-Lances are robotic humanoid Darkners residing in the Cyber World. Their pill-shaped bodies display red and blue patterns with a prominent cross symbol on the front. A syringe serves as their head, featuring two angry yellow eyes and a rotating police siren on top. They wield reflex hammers as weapons. Functionally acting as antivirus programs, they aggressively pursue Virovirokun - whom they perceive as infectious computer viruses - employing a mix of medical and law enforcement jargon in their confrontational dialogue.

entries.name: Plugboy
entries.content: Plugboys are small humanoid Darkners inhabiting the Cyber Field and occasionally Cyber City. Their distinctive feature is a face shaped as a NEMA 5-15R electrical socket. Their bodies display various colors, each possessing two stubby horns atop their heads. Plugboys serve as common citizens within the Cyber World's ecosystem. They transform into Werewires when exposed to Queen's specialized connection wires interfacing directly with their cranial sockets.

entries.name: Werewire
entries.content: The Werewires, Queen's transformed Plugboys, stand as unsettling anomalies within the Cyber World. Their pink and blue fuzzy bodies flop with each motion, limbs swaying erratically above green stripes. A constant thick wire latches onto their face, visible just below the pink neck ruffle. Queen's control forces them into a perpetual lethargy, described as sleepwalking through a nightmare with no free will. Non-hostile variants exist, subdued and listless. In combat, they shriek in electric static while launching electronic projectiles. Disconnecting their facial plug reverts them to harmless Plugboys.

entries.name: Werewerewire
entries.content: Werewerewires are enhanced variants of Werewires distinguished by dark purple bodies with cyan accents and a prominent white fur collar. They possess a drill-shaped mask instead of a face plug and show no visible eyes. These entities absorbed their control wires through sheer willpower, retaining autonomy without reverting to Plugboys when spared. Their mentality emphasizes combat superiority; they interpret mercy as insulting weakness and refuse communication beyond battle. Strong-willed and silent, they prioritize victory above all else.

entries.name: Sweet
entries.content:
Sweet is a Darkner from the Cyber World resembling a dual-stacked mono speaker system. He is part of the Sweet Cap'n Cakes
musical trio.  The upper speaker features a speaker cap functioning as its eye, marked by a single golden iris and pupil. Solid black arms with yellow gloves extend from the lower speaker. Attire includes a forward-facing black hat, dark gray headphones with gold accents, black pants with two gold button-like dials, black shoes with gold laces and blue soles, and white socks with gold trim.

entries.name: Cap'n
entries.content: Cap'n is a Darkner from the Cyber World resembling a cassette player. He is part of the musical trio Sweet Cap'n Cakes. His head functions as a cassette deck with headphone jacks serving as ears. Attire includes a backward purple cap, yellow headphones decorated with musical eighth notes, sunglasses, a blue short-sleeved hoodie, and a purple bandana. Solid black arms end in yellow gloves. He wears black pants with a purple belt, and purple shoes with white laces and soles.

entries.name: K_K (Cakes)
entries.content: K_K is a Darkner from the Cyber World resembling a stacked CD player system. He is part of the musical trio Sweet Cap'n Cakes. His head is green with gold eyes and a purple handle. A black, green-striped spine extends from his white boombox body. His attire includes green pants with a belt loop, black boots with gold laces and green soles, and gold bracelets on both wrists. As the rhythm keeper of the trio, he communicates in clipped phrases emphasizing rhythm and flow.

entries.name: Sweet Cap'n' Cakes
entries.content: Sweet Cap'n Cakes is a rebellious musical trio composed of Sweet (a mono speaker Darkner with a speaker cap functioning as an eye), Cap'n (a cassette player Darkner with headphone ears), and K_K (a CD player Darkner with green features). They run a chaotic shop in the Cyber Field in the Cyber World filled with CD Bagels and salvaged electronics. Their primary motivation is resisting Queen's music ban through impromptu dance-offs and loud jam sessions, though their plans often derail into arguments or distractions. Each member communicates rhythmically, prioritizing beats over coherent strategy.

entries.name: Muffet
entries.content:
Muffet is a slender anthropomorphic spider running her bakery in Hometown. Her appearance features deep purple skin and six dexterous arms. She wears a purple minidress under a white apron with magenta accents. Her sharp fangs and five purple eyes convey playful menace, enhanced by dark freckles dotting her cheeks.

Behaviorally, Muffet presents a facade of sweet politeness to mask ruthless greed. She exploits customers through predatory pricing and secret venom additives ensuring addiction. Her genuine care surfaces only toward fellow spiders, channeling profits into arachnid welfare. She seeks eventual financial dominance to establish a sovereign spider kingdom free from discrimination.

Muffet migrated to Hometown after facing persecution in her mountain village. Her bakery serves as both business front and residence. She employs non-sapient spiders as assistants and keeps the pet "Muffin" confined after an attack incident. Her ultimate ambition remains acquiring a mansion through any means necessary.

entries.name: Mr. "Ant" Tenna
entries.content:
Mr. Tenna is a humanoid Darkner with a cuboid television head modeled after the Dreemurr residence's TV. His eyeless face features a long nose, and his pre-rendered 3D model-like body shifts in size with emotional intensity. He wears a red tailcoat with a golden "TV" emblem over a white shirt and yellow tie, paired with black pants secured by a TV-shaped belt and yellow shoes with black soles. White gloves complete his announcer aesthetic.

Mr. Tenna embodies manic showmanship as host of TV Time—energetic, joke-prone, and desperate for approval. Beneath his bombastic persona lies crippling insecurity, manifesting in coercive tactics to retain Lightner "contestants" through contractual traps or distractions. He enforces oppressive labor contracts on TV World Darkners to maintain control, driven by fear of obsolescence. Though nominally serving the Knight to safeguard his Dark Fountain, his loyalty stems from promises of perpetual relevance through captive audiences.

Tenna knows Spamton, and used to work with him towards making him famous - being the epiphomous person behind the phone. One day their relationship soured, and Tenna ceased contact with Spamton, causing their relationship to collapse and for Spamton's downfall to begin.

entries.name: Ramb
entries.content:
Ramb is a Plugboy Darkner in the TV World distinguished by bluish-purple coloration and downward-curving ears. His orange apron contrasts with the standard Plugboy design. Though perpetually smiling, he adopts smug expressions when addressing personal topics, particularly with Kris. As he is not native to the TV World, he is very slowly growing through petrification.

Behaviorally, Ramb exudes sass and superiority, speaking in a British accent. Being an outsider, he is alienated him from other TV World Darkners. He maintains secret knowledge of Kris' past, referencing shared history through veiled nostalgia. His prize counter operation masks deeper motives - hosting an illicit backstage arcade cabinet running the unaltered "Legend of Tenna" game to subvert Tenna's authority. His loyalty lies solely with Kris, prioritizing their interests over TV World hierarchy despite his surface-level compliance as a shopkeeper for Tenna.

entries.name: Lanino
entries.content:
Lanino is a flamboyant Darkner co-host in the TV World, distinguished by his yellow crescent moon-shaped head and fiery orange pompadour resembling stylized cloud formations. His sleek dark blue suit and pants contrast sharply with vibrant red gloves and pointed shoes. Shoulder flames flicker perpetually without burning fabric. He wields a white wand tipped with an upward-pointing index finger.

Behaviorally, Lanino radiates theatrical arrogance, delivering weather-themed puns with manic energy. His partnership with Elnina blends romantic tension and competitive showmanship, often devolving into jealous outbursts when her attention wavers. His attacks utilize solar projectiles and localized heatwaves. Despite his bombastic hosting duties under Tenna, his fragile ego requires constant validation through audience cheers and Elnina’s admiration.

entries.name: Elnina
entries.content:
Elnina is a dramatic Darkner co-host in the TV World, recognizable by her cerulean skin, cloud-like white twin-tails, and a gradient skirt mimicking stormy skies. Her oversized sunglasses and yellow galoshes complete her chaotic weathercaster aesthetic.

Elnina thrives on melodramatic flair, delivering meteorological puns with breathless intensity. Her partnership with Lanino mixes volatile romantic chemistry and cutthroat rivalry, erupting into tearful tantrums when upstaged. Attacks conjure torrential rains and hail barrages. Though desperate for viewer adoration, her fragile self-worth hinges on Lanino's fickle admiration and Tenna's approval, masking her deep-seated insecurity beneath her performative confidence.

entries.name: Pippins
entries.content: Pippins are diamond-shaped Darkners in the TV World modeled after six-sided dice. Their white hexagonal heads feature red eyes and wide mouths, with bodies encased in red overcoats over black shirts and white collars with red ties. Three-pointed gloved fingers protrude from their sleeves, matching their black pants. Obsessed with gambling, Pippins flout rules frequently—earning disdain from orderly Darkners like Zappers and Tenna. They communicate through exaggerated dice-themed puns and gestures, thriving on chaotic risk-taking despite the consequences. They are one of the main Darkners found in the TV World, and are a rare sight in the Card Kingdom as well.

entries.name: Shadowguy
entries.content: Shadowguys are humanoid Darkners in the TV World resembling black silhouettes with white outlines, styled as 1920s mobsters. Their broad-shouldered forms wear fedoras and trenchcoats, occasionally swapping hats for striped socks or animal ears during performances. Faceless and mute, they communicate through jazz riffs. Shadowguys serve as enthusiastic studio audiences and stagehands for TV Time, moving in coordinated groups to clap, cheer, or adjust sets. Their attacks involve synchronized dance numbers summoning musical notes and instruments and firing projectiles with guns resembling Tommy Guns. Despite their ominous appearance, they exude playful energy, thriving on showmanship and rhythm. They are one of the most numerous Darkner types in the TV World, especially in the audiences of TV Time.

entries.name: Zapper
entries.content:
Zappers are humanoid Darkners in the TV World resembling television remotes. Their elongated navy blue bodies have a red sensor light at the crown and lack facial features despite blushing capability. White shoulder pads and red gloves accentuate their formal navy suits featuring six triangular buttons (three red, three white). They balance on a single leg, bouncing rhythmically during confrontations with perpetually outstretched palms.

Zappers serve as Tenna’s security enforcers, divided into two behavioral archetypes: brash "button-men" using mobster vernacular and refined "gentlemen" employing polite threats. Both types coordinate to eject disruptive guests from studio sets through synchronized shockwave attacks emitted from their sensor lights.

entries.name: Shuttah
entries.content:
Shuttahs are humanoid Darkners in the TV World resembling animated camera shutters. Their bodies feature vertical red, yellow, green, and blue stripes ending in high-heeled feet. A grinning mouth shaped like film strips sits atop their torso, while two large yellow-rimmed eyes extend from their elongated arms. They strike exaggerated poses during combat.

Shuttahs are eccentric and theatrical, addressing foes with affectionate terms like "darling" while praising photogenic qualities. Their attacks involve camera flash bursts and pose-inspired energy projections. Nostalgic by nature, they frequently reference past events or aesthetics mid-battle. Despite aggressive posturing, they view conflicts as collaborative performance art.

entries.name: Ribbick
entries.content: Ribbicks are frog-like Darkners in the TV World with pale green skin and long whiskers protruding from their cheeks. Their eyes remain perpetually closed, giving them a lethargic appearance. They hop erratically while croaking nonsensical phrases, mirroring Rabbick's nonsensical behavior. Like their rabbit counterparts, they can be pacified by blowing on them, causing their whiskers to twitch contentedly despite lacking visible mouths.

entries.name: Watercooler
entries.content: Watercoolers are stationary Darkners resembling standard office water dispensers. Their gray bases feature red and blue buttons beside cup dispensers, topped with blue 5-gallon jugs containing glowing liquid. Though seemingly inanimate, they possess latent sentience, communicating through distorted "bubble" misspellings. Originally Mizzles transformed by Mr. Tenna, their true nature is masked by mundane appearances. Despite their passive role as hydration stations, Watercoolers radiate an inexplicable, overwhelming aura of dread that unsettles even seasoned Darkners. Their motives remain unclear, though some theorize their presence enforces subconscious obedience through psychological pressure.

entries.name: Shadow Mantle Holder
entries.content: Shadow Mantle Holder is a pixelated boss in the TV World's hidden "Original Version" of Legend of Tenna. Its form resembles a black hooded cloak with jagged horns and a glowing orange mouth. The entity taunts players through distorted text boxes, ridiculing their pursuit of Shadow Crystals and "fun" as futile traps. Defeating it causes the Shadow Mantle - a cursed cloak granting invisibility - to materialize in the real world while permanently corrupting the game cartridge into an unplayable state. Its mocking dialogue implies awareness of the player's meta-narrative role.

entries.name: Father Alvin
entries.content:
Father Alvin is a green-skinned turtle monster serving as Hometown's chaplain. His rounded shell and pink eyebrows frame gentle brown eyes, with long pink hair flowing over traditional blue clerical robes bearing the Delta Rune emblem. He maintains an upright posture, hands perpetually clasped near his chest in quiet contemplation.

Alvin embodies compassionate spirituality, guiding parishioners with soft-spoken wisdom and an open heart. Though deeply devoted to his father Gerson Boom's legacy, he struggles privately with insecurities about measuring up to his father's reputation. His sermons emphasize community and kindness, delivered with a reassuring calm occasionally lightened by subtle humor. Beneath his serene demeanor lies quiet determination to honor tradition while forging his own path through service.

entries.name: Gerson Boom (Light World)
entries.content:
Gerson Boom was a green-skinned turtle monster with distinctive pink hair and beard flowing past his sturdy frame. His right eye remained perpetually shut, lending him a weathered but approachable appearance.

Gerson served as Hometown's beloved schoolteacher before Alphys, known for his bravery, sharp intellect, and laid-back demeanor. He uplifted students through warm support and self-deprecating humor about his advancing age. Originally working as a blacksmith, he transitioned to writing—first gaining renown as a historian before achieving fame with his award-winning fantasy novel series Lord of the Hammer. This series grew from stories he crafted to entertain his children. He passed away approximately ten years ago, leaving behind a legacy fondly looked back on by his son Alvin and Hometown's older residents.

entries.name: Asriel Dreemurr (Returned)
entries.content:
Asriel Dreemurr is a 6'0" anthropomorphic goat Lightner and honors student at college. His lithe athletic build is covered in smooth white fur, accented by short curved horns and a modest tail. He favors practical attire like olive track jackets layered over cotton shirts, though his Dark World form features black-and-white robes with silver pauldrons and black sclera.

Asriel projects gentle authority through academic drive and conflict mediation, masking chronic guilt over abandoning younger sibling Kris during familial collapse. Clinging to being an acaemic prodigy, he compulsively prioritizes others' needs while neglecting personal boundaries. Underlying anxiety manifests as nervous habits like paw-fidgeting and stammering during emotional confrontations. He maintains strained relationships through performative cheerfulness, privately fearing rejection from those he failed.

Kris is Asriel's adoptive sibling. Toriel and Asgore are his parents. He used to be romantic partners with December Holiday before her disappearance.
